sourceNote: Names are reconstructed Proto-Germanic. 'runePoem' paraphrases the Old English Rune Poem unless marked (ON = Old Norwegian, OI = Old Icelandic). 'modernAssociations' are mostly 20th-century and are labelled as such in the UI. The Elder Futhark was primarily a writing system. Order of the last two runes varies between inscriptions.

runes.name: Fehu
runes.runePoem: Wealth is a comfort to all, yet each must share it freely.
runes.reflectionPrompt: What do you have that feels like enough today? What would you like to share?

runes.name: Uruz
runes.runePoem: The aurochs is fierce and great-horned, a bold moor-stepper.
runes.reflectionPrompt: Where in your body do you feel strong right now, even a little?

runes.name: Thurisaz
runes.literalMeaning: giant (Norse þurs); the Old English poem names it 'thorn'
runes.runePoem: The thorn is very sharp, painful to anyone who grasps it.
runes.reflectionPrompt: Which of your boundaries has been protecting you? Can you thank it?

runes.name: Ansuz
runes.literalMeaning: a god (one of the Æsir); the Old English poem names it 'mouth'
runes.runePoem: The mouth is the source of all speech, a support of wisdom.
runes.reflectionPrompt: Is there something one part of you is trying to say to another?

runes.name: Raidō
runes.runePoem: Riding seems easy to warriors indoors, but hard on a strong horse on the long road.
runes.reflectionPrompt: What's one small step on the road you're on?

runes.name: Kaunan / Kenaz
runes.runePoem: The torch is known to every living thing by its pale, bright flame.
runes.reflectionPrompt: What feels a little clearer than it did before?

runes.name: Gebō
runes.runePoem: Generosity brings credit and honour, and support to the destitute.
runes.reflectionPrompt: What has someone, maybe someone inside, given you lately?

runes.name: Wunjō
runes.runePoem: Joy belongs to one who knows little sorrow, and has prosperity and a good enough house.
runes.reflectionPrompt: Name one small thing that brought you joy this week.

runes.name: Hagalaz
runes.runePoem: Hail is the whitest of grain. It whirls from the sky, then turns to water.
runes.reflectionPrompt: Hail melts into water. What hard thing might soften with time?

runes.name: Naudiz
runes.runePoem: Need is tight on the chest, yet it can bring help and healing if heeded early.
runes.reflectionPrompt: What do you need right now? Can anyone, inside or outside, help with it?

runes.name: Īsaz
runes.runePoem: Ice is very cold and slippery, glistening like glass, a floor made by frost.
runes.reflectionPrompt: Sometimes freezing is protection. What would help you thaw, gently?

runes.name: Jēra
runes.runePoem: Harvest is the hope of all, when the earth gives her bright fruits.
runes.reflectionPrompt: What have you planted that is slowly growing?

runes.name: Eihwaz
runes.runePoem: The yew has rough bark, held firm in the earth, a keeper of fire.
runes.reflectionPrompt: What keeps you rooted when things shake?

runes.name: Perþō
runes.literalMeaning: uncertain; possibly a lot-cup or a game piece
runes.runePoem: Peorð is play and laughter among the proud, where warriors sit in the beer-hall.
runes.reflectionPrompt: Not everything needs to be known yet. What can you let stay a mystery for now?
runes.contextNote: The meaning of this rune's name is genuinely unknown to scholars.

runes.name: Algiz
runes.literalMeaning: uncertain; often reconstructed as 'elk' or 'protection'; the Old English poem names elk-sedge
runes.runePoem: Elk-sedge grows in the marsh; it wounds and burns anyone who grasps it.
runes.reflectionPrompt: Who or what are your protectors? How do they show care?
runes.contextNote: This rune has been misused by some white supremacist groups. The game presents it only in historical and linguistic context.

runes.name: Sōwilō
runes.runePoem: The sun is a joy and hope to seafarers crossing the fishes' bath.
runes.reflectionPrompt: Where is the light coming from today, however faint?
runes.contextNote: Doubled, angular stylizations were used by Nazi organizations. The game never uses those forms.

runes.name: Tīwaz
runes.runePoem: Tir is a guiding sign that keeps faith well, always on its course through the night's mists.
runes.reflectionPrompt: What value do you want to steer by, even in the fog?
runes.contextNote: This rune has been misused by some extremist groups. The game uses only the historical form and context.

runes.name: Berkanan
runes.runePoem: The birch (or poplar) bears no fruit, yet sends out shoots; its branches are beautiful.
runes.reflectionPrompt: What part of you needs gentle tending right now?

runes.name: Ehwaz
runes.runePoem: The horse is a joy to nobles; to the restless it is a comfort.
runes.reflectionPrompt: Who do you move through life alongside? What makes that partnership work?

runes.name: Mannaz
runes.runePoem: Each person is dear to their kin, yet all must one day part.
runes.reflectionPrompt: What does 'I' mean to you today? What does 'we' mean?

runes.name: Laguz
runes.runePoem: The sea seems endless to those who venture out on it.
runes.reflectionPrompt: If your feelings were water today, would they be still, flowing or stormy?

runes.name: Ingwaz
runes.runePoem: Ing was first seen among the East-Danes, then went eastward over the waves.
runes.reflectionPrompt: What's quietly growing inside you that isn't ready to be seen yet?

runes.name: Dagaz
runes.runePoem: Day is the Lord's messenger, dear to all; a hope and help to rich and poor.
runes.reflectionPrompt: What would a slightly better morning look like for all of you?

runes.name: Ōþila
runes.runePoem: An estate is dear to everyone who can enjoy what is right and proper in their home.
runes.reflectionPrompt: Home can be something you build. What makes a place feel safe to you?
runes.contextNote: A 'winged' variant was used by Nazi units and is still used by hate groups. The game uses only the plain historical glyph, and the Codex notes that inclusive heathen communities reject this misuse.
